title: Charge-4e Superconducting Ground State without Pair Condensation: Exact Quartet Dynamics, Rigorous Order, and a Microscopic Route
authors: Jin-Tao Jin, Pengfei Li, Yi Zhou
abstract: A direct charge-\(4e\) superconductor exhibits coherent four-electron order while every charge-\(2e\) pairing channel remains uncondensed. We establish three complementary results. First, building on the \(η\)-clustering states and bipartite parent of Yoshida and Katsura, we formulate and exactly solve a minimal two-term parent on any connected graph. Its fixed-number ground states have quartet off-diagonal long-range order (ODLRO) without charge-\(2e\) ODLRO, while an exact mapping to classical hard-core exclusion dynamics yields the full fixed-sector gap and a branch of quartet-density modes. Nonzero quartet stiffness and vanishing inverse quartet compressibility identify this \(z=2\) parent as a phase-separation boundary. Second, for a finite-range fermionic family with explicit quartet transfer and sufficiently large onsite penalty, we rigorously prove quartet ODLRO without charge-\(2e\) ODLRO at half quartet filling, both at the hypercubic XY point for \(d\geq2\) and throughout a finite XXZ interval on the square lattice. Third, we derive a strong-coupling realization using only electron hopping and two-body interactions. With local gap \(U_0\), pair hopping \(K\) generates quartet motion at order \(K^2/U_0\), whereas electron hopping \(t\) first contributes at order \(t^4/U_0^3\); charge-\(2e\) excitations remain gapped at \(O(U_0)\). On bipartite lattices, positive inverse quartet compressibility opens an asymptotically controlled homogeneous \(z=1\) regime with short-ranged pair correlations, while negative curvature drives phase separation.
summary: This paper establishes the theoretical existence of a charge-4e superconducting ground state that maintains robust four-electron order while suppressing conventional two-electron pairing condensation. Using exact solutions and strong-coupling expansions, the authors provide rigorous proofs and microscopic derivations demonstrating this exotic superconducting phase stability.
main_problem: The paper addresses the theoretical challenge of establishing a superconducting ground state characterized by coherent charge-4e order while ensuring that lower-charge pairing channels (charge-2e) remain uncondensed.
main_result: The authors rigorously prove the existence of a charge-4e superconducting phase exhibiting quartet Off-Diagonal Long-Range Order (ODLRO) without charge-2e ODLRO, even deriving its stability from microscopic hopping terms.
method: The analysis employs exact solutions for minimal parent Hamiltonians, strong-coupling perturbation theory, and rigorous mathematical bounds (like the linked-cluster argument) to diagnose order and stability.
model_or_system: The study focuses on a direct charge-4e superconductor modeled using parent Hamiltonians defined on connected graphs, which are subsequently analyzed via effective low-energy Hamiltonians resembling XXZ models.

paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first solving a minimal parent Hamiltonian exactly, establishing the quartet ODLRO. It then proves the result for a finite-range fermionic model using rigorous theorems, and finally derives a strong-coupling microscopic realization using electron hopping and pair hopping terms.
why_interesting: The work provides a highly detailed, mathematically rigorous framework for stabilizing higher-order superconducting phases (charge-4e) against competing lower-order instabilities (charge-2e), which is crucial for understanding exotic superconductivity in correlated materials.
